newsitem.title: UK: Utd News sells Welsh papers to Southern.
newsitem.headline: Utd News sells Welsh papers to Southern.

text.p: United News & Media said on Monday it had sold the Welsh division of its regional newspaper subsidiary to Southern Newspapers for 31.5 million stg.
It said discussions about the sale of its regional newspapers in south-east England were continuing.

United News said the proceeds from the sale would be used to reduce group indebtedness. It announced in August that it planned to divest the Wales and South East divisions of its United Provincial Newspapers subsidiary.
The decision was taken as part of its review of operations following its merger with MAI earlier this year. It plans to focus on its core regions of Yorkshire and north-west England.
The Welsh division publishes a range of titles including the South Wales Argus. In 1995 it reported operating profits of 1.08 million stg on turnover of 15.15 million.
The deal moves Southern Newspapers from 11th to ninth place in the table of the UK's top regional publishers.

"This is a significant move for Southern Newspapers and is part of our ongoing strategy to expand the group through the acquisition of additional titles," said James Sexton, Southern Newspapers' chief executive.
